claims.title: Selected digit gaps control repetition, branching and distinguishability

plain_language.question: How does choosing which binary digits to count change an infinite pattern?
plain_language.what_we_learned: Exact formulas determine its factor counts and strongest repetitions; a complete branching-pattern classification explains the changes, and the full count function identifies the chosen digit positions.

claims.exact_statement_and_scope: Let S={0=s_0<s_1<…} be any infinite set of binary positions and x_S(r) the XOR of r's bits in S. Put A_i=2^(s_i), A_0=1. Its complexity satisfies p_S(0)=1; p_S(L)=2L for 1≤L≤A_1+1; for i≥1, p_S(L)=4L−2(A_i−A_{i−1}+2) on A_i+2≤L≤2A_i−A_{i−1}+1, and p_S(L)=2L+2(A_i−1) on 2A_i−A_{i−1}+2≤L≤A_{i+1}+1. These ranges cover all positive L; differences at L≥2 are 2 or 4. The exact critical exponent is sup_{i≥1}2^(s_i−s_{i−1}), including infinity. Every nonempty bispecial factor has the edition's unique desubstitution description as an alternating-word image, with full extension classification; strong lengths are 2^(s_{i+1}), weak lengths 2^(s_{i+1}+1)−2^(s_i). For L≥1, 2L≤p_S(L)≤p_TM(L). If S,T first differ in membership at position r≥1, their first differing count is at L=2^r+2, differing by 2, so the full complexity function determines S. For finite mask m with S_m={p:p AND m=0}, E=2^(m+1); masks first differing in bit r first differ in count at L=2^(2^r)+2.

claims.title: Every finite prefix can exist without one positive infinite realization

plain_language.question: Can one positive Collatz start follow a fixed Thue–Morse arrangement of valuation blocks forever?
plain_language.what_we_learned: Only if that same start lies on a cycle. In two specified growing code families, even that exception is impossible, although every finite prefix remains positively realizable.
plain_language.what_it_lets_someone_do: Exclude a concrete infinite-code construction using its repetition structure rather than an arbitrary computation cutoff.
plain_language.what_cannot_conclude: This does not prove Collatz, exclude arbitrary aperiodic valuation codes, or rule out every nontrivial positive cycle.

claims.exact_statement_and_scope: Use the fully accelerated odd map U(n)=(3n+1)/2^(v_2(3n+1)) on positive odd integers. Let t be ordinary binary Thue–Morse starting 0 and let B_0,B_1 be any fixed nonempty finite words of positive integer valuations. If B_{t_0}B_{t_1}… is the exact valuation sequence of one positive odd N, then U^j(N)=N for some j>0. No equal-codeword-length or average-valuation hypothesis is assumed. The special code B_0=(1),B_1=(2), and every fixed pair B_0=1^p3,B_1=1^q3 with p,q≥3, admit no positive realization because their selected returns strictly grow. The cycle exception is essential: B_0=B_1=(2),N=1 realizes the general premise. Equal length-2d valuation prefixes returning at accelerated time 3d with distinct states require 2·32^d<27^d(N+1); balanced Thue–Morse returns provide unbounded d. The full theorem is analytic, with narrower formal collision/numerical components.
